title: Research: an app-held pane pool with a queue and a 4-running cap
notes:
Research, no branch. The user's idea: main asks the app to launch a pane; the app keeps a pool, runs at most 4 at once, queues the rest and starts the next the moment one frees, so main no longer tracks slots.

Review it thoroughly against the code (pane claim/run, board ship, pr land release, pane finish, worker states running/paused/done in src/main/workers, budget) and propose a design. Questions to settle with examples: what holds a slot (a paused worker waiting on CI, a review loop, a done-but-kept pane); queue order and how main reorders or withdraws an entry, including file-overlap between a queued card and an open PR; global across projects or per project; budget gating before each start; what the queued caller gets back (an id now, a notice at start); what happens to the queue across an app restart; how the cap is set (settings file). Say what can be deleted from main's instructions once it exists.

comments.body: Review done, report at /tmp/pane-pool-review.md. Sound idea: every agent start already goes through pane.dispatch, and no cap exists in code today (the 4 rule lives only in main's conversation; c5b8a687's 8-worker OOM is the motivation). Design: one app-wide pool, cap workers.cap in settings.json (default 4). Gate the new-work doors only (new pane start, board ship, review sweep); restore, pane send and New Claude are never queued. A slot is held by running, blocked and paused (hook can't tell a CI wait from a test run); done and kept panes free it. FIFO plus --first, pane queue, pane unqueue, and --after <card> for file overlap (the app can't know a queued card's files). Pane and worktree are picked at start, never at queue time (freePaneIn would hand a reserved shell to a ship). Budget is checked in the app before each start, with 'no limit set' as no gate (default weeklyCap null makes budget exit 2). Start answers at once with started/queued q7, then a notice at start. Queue persisted to pane-queue.json. Deletes from main's prompt: claim+run, the 10-minute timeout, the budget-before-each-round paragraph, the slot counting.
